ai.literal: Having thought, one thing won't you say, O heart? Any whatsoever distress-disease curing medicine.
ai.translation: O heart, think carefully and tell me one thing: is there any medicine whatsoever that can cure this grievous disease?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே, எனது இந்தத் துன்ப நோயைத் தீர்க்கக்கூடிய மருந்து ஏதாவது ஒன்றாவது இருக்கிறதா என்று சிந்தித்து எனக்குச் சொல்வாயாக.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, overwhelmed by the pain of separation. She asks her heart to think deeply and suggest at least one remedy that could cure her intense suffering. The word 'எவ்வநோய்' refers to the grievous disease of love-sickness, while 'எனைத்தொன்றும்' emphasizes her desperate search for absolutely any cure. By pleading with her heart, she highlights her helplessness and the unbearable nature of her longing.

ai.literal: Love he is without as it is, you aching is foolishness, may you live, my heart!
ai.translation: My heart, may you live! Since he has no love for us, it is foolishness for you to suffer.
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சே, நீ வாழ்வாயாக! அவர் நம்மிடம் காதல் இல்லாதவராக இருக்க, நீ மட்டும் அவருக்காகத் துன்பப்படுவது அறியாமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart, pointing out the one-sided nature of her affection. She notes that her lover does not possess the same love for her. Therefore, she tells her heart that its continued aching and suffering for him is pure foolishness. The blessing 'may you live' is a gentle, pitying address to her own distressed mind.

ai.literal: Sitting and thinking, why grieve, O heart? Thinking with pity is not with those who caused sorrowful pain.
ai.translation: O my heart, why sit and grieve, constantly thinking of him? The one who caused this sorrowful pain has no pitying thought for us.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! அவர் நினைவாகவே இருந்து ஏன் வருந்துகிறாய்? இந்தத் துன்ப நோயை நமக்குத் தந்தவரிடம், நம்மீது இரக்கப்பட்டு நினைக்கும் குணம் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, questioning its constant sorrow. She asks why it sits and grieves, constantly thinking of her lover. She reminds her heart that the lover, who caused her this distressing pain of separation, does not have the compassion to think of her in return. The contrast is between her constant, painful remembering ('இருந்து உள்ளி') and his complete lack of sympathetic thought ('பரிந்து உள்ளல் இல்').

ai.literal: Eyes too to take you go, O heart! These me will eat, him seeing having desired.
ai.translation: O heart, take my eyes along when you go to him. Otherwise, desiring to see him, they will eat me alive.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! நீ அவரிடம் செல்லும்போது என் கண்களையும் உடன் அழைத்துச் செல். இல்லையென்றால், அவரைக் காண விரும்பி இந்தக் கண்கள் என்னைத் தின்றுவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, which is rushing to be with her lover. She begs her heart to take her eyes along on the journey. If left behind, her eyes, consumed by the intense desire to see him, will torment her endlessly, as if eating her alive. The word 'தின்னும்' (will eat) vividly captures the physical pain and relentless nature of her unfulfilled visual longing.

ai.literal: Those who hate, saying, abandoning is there, O heart, we, if loved, those who do not love.
ai.translation: O heart, is it possible to abandon him saying 'he hates us', when he does not return our love even as we love him?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! நாம் அன்பு செலுத்தினாலும் நம்மிடம் அன்பு செலுத்தாத அவரை, அவர் நம்மை வெறுக்கிறார் என்று கூறி நாம் கைவிடுவது சாத்தியமா?
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart, which is drawn to her lover despite his apparent indifference. She asks if it is truly possible to abandon him just because he seems to shun them. The contrast between 'யாம் உற்றால்' (when we love) and 'உறாஅதவர்' (he who does not love) highlights her unrequited yet unwavering affection. The rhetorical question 'கைவிடல் உண்டோ' implies that letting go is entirely impossible for her.

ai.literal: having united / who pacifies / lover / if seen / having sulked / you do not realize / false / anger / you are angry / my / heart
ai.translation: O my heart, you are burning with a false anger! For if you see our lover who embraces and pacifies us, you will not hold on to your sulking.
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சே! கூடி மகிழ்ந்து நம்மை சமாதானப்படுத்தும் காதலரைக் கண்டால் நீ ஊடல் கொண்டு நிற்கமாட்டாய்; அதனால் இப்போது நீ கொள்ளும் கோபம் பொய்யானதே.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, pointing out the futility of its current anger towards her absent lover. She calls the heart's anger 'false' (பொய் காய்வு) because she knows it will instantly vanish the moment the lover returns. When he embraces and pacifies her (கலந்து உணர்த்தும்), the heart will completely forget to sulk (புலந்து உணராய்), proving its present resentment is merely a temporary pretense.

ai.literal: Desire give up either one, shame give up, O good heart! As for me, I cannot bear these two.
ai.translation: O my good heart, give up your desire or give up your shame. As for me, I cannot bear the burden of these two together.
ai.modern: நல்ல நெஞ்சமே! நீ காமத்தையாவது விட்டுவிடு, அல்லது நாணத்தையாவது விட்டுவிடு. என்னால் இவை இரண்டையும் சேர்த்துத் தாங்கிக்கொள்ள முடியாது.
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her heart, which is struggling between two conflicting emotions. On one hand, she feels intense desire for her lover, which urges her to seek him out. On the other hand, she feels modesty or shame, which holds her back. She tells her heart to choose one and abandon the other, because she herself lacks the strength to endure the heavy burden of both at the same time.

ai.literal: He-who-loved will-not-grant-[favor] thinking having-yearned, he-who-parted behind you-will-go, foolish my heart.
ai.translation: O my foolish heart! Yearning with the thought that he who once loved you will no longer show you grace, you go chasing after the one who departed.
ai.modern: அன்பு செய்தவர் இனி அருள் செய்ய மாட்டார் என்று ஏங்கி, உன்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்றவரின் பின்னால் நீ செல்கிறாய், என் அறிவற்ற நெஞ்சே.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, calling it foolish. She notes that her heart yearns in fear that her lover, who once showed great affection, will no longer grant his grace. Driven by this sorrowful longing, the heart abandons her and chases after the very person who departed. The word 'pētai' (foolish) highlights the heart's irrationality in pursuing someone who has already chosen to leave.

ai.literal: In the heart he is, the lover being; thinking, you, who near do you go, my heart?
ai.translation: My heart, the lover is already inside you. Yet you think of him and go searching. To whose place are you going?
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சே! காதலர் உனக்குள்ளேயே இருக்க, அவரை நினைத்து நீ யாரிடம் செல்கிறாய்?
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, which is longing for her lover and seems to wander in search of him. She reminds her heart that the lover is already residing within it. Since he is ever-present inside, she asks her heart where else it could possibly go to find him. The word 'உள்ளத்தார்' (he is inside) contrasts with 'யார் உழைச் சேறி' (to whose place do you go), highlighting the irony of searching outside for what is already within.

ai.literal: Without approaching, him who left, in heart do we possess? Still we will lose beauty.
ai.translation: Do we still hold in our heart the lover who left us without an embrace? If so, we will only lose our beauty even more.
ai.modern: நம்மை நெருங்காமல் பிரிந்து சென்றவரை நாம் இன்னும் நெஞ்சில் கொண்டிருக்கிறோமா? அப்படியானால் நாம் நமது அழகை இன்னும் இழந்துவிடுவோம்.
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart in a moment of deep sorrow over her unrequited longing. She questions why they still hold onto the memory of a lover who abandoned them without showing any closeness or affection. She realizes that keeping him constantly in her thoughts will only cause her to pine away and lose whatever beauty she has left.
